name: python3
one_line: Use `python3 -c` for the small decode, convert and brute-force jobs that come up in every CTF.
plain: Use `python3 -c` for the small decode, convert and brute-force jobs that come up in every CTF.
The sections below show when to use it, real examples, and the options explained in plain English.
when: Decode or encode base64, hex, URL or binary text.
Convert between number bases and byte orders.
XOR, hash, brute-force a short secret, or work out tiny RSA.
Parse a log with Counter instead of building a long shell pipeline.

examples.title: XOR with a repeating key
examples.cmd: python3 -c "d=bytes.fromhex('0b0d080c'); k=b'AB'; print(bytes(b ^ k[i % len(k)] for i, b in enumerate(d)))"

examples.title: Number bases
examples.cmd: python3 -c "n=0xdeadbeef; print(n); print(bin(10), oct(64), hex(255)); print(int('777', 8), int('1010', 2), int('ff', 16))"

examples.title: Byte order (endianness)
examples.cmd: python3 -c "import struct; print(struct.pack('<I', 0xdeadbeef).hex(), struct.pack('>I', 0xdeadbeef).hex()); print(hex(struct.unpack('<I', bytes.fromhex('efbeadde'))[0]))"

examples.title: Brute-force a short secret from its hash
examples.cmd: python3 -c "import hashlib, itertools; t = hashlib.md5(b'4821').hexdigest(); print(t); print(next(''.join(c) for c in itertools.product('0123456789', repeat=4) if hashlib.md5(''.join(c).encode()).hexdigest() == t))"

examples.title: Count things in a log
examples.cmd: python3 -c "import collections; print(collections.Counter(l.split()[0] for l in open('access.log')).most_common(2))"

examples.title: Tiny RSA
examples.cmd: python3 -c "p, q, e = 61, 53, 17; n = p * q; d = pow(e, -1, (p - 1) * (q - 1)); m = 65; c = pow(m, e, n); print(n, d, c, pow(c, d, n))"

options.plain: Hex string to bytes and back
Pack a number as little-endian bytes (`>` = big-endian)
Every combination of a character set

mistakes: Quote carefully: wrap the program in double quotes in bash and use single quotes inside (or the other way round).
Integer division is `//`; `/` gives a float, which breaks big-number maths.
For anything longer than three lines, write a file and add comments.
try: Decode a base64 string, then hex-decode the result.
XOR two hex strings of equal length.
Find the PIN whose sha1 equals a hash of your choice.
see_also: CyberChef, xxd, base64, pwntools, pycryptodome, sympy, z3.
